$comment: Language runtimes pre-installed into the Piston container.
This is the execution matrix the platform supports. It is deliberately a
data file rather than a shell script so that packages/exec-adapter can
read the same list and reject a language the sandbox cannot run, instead
of discovering it at grading time when a candidate is already waiting.
VERSION PINNING. The `version` values below are the targets. Piston
resolves them against its own package index, which carries specific patch
releases and does not always have the newest one. install-runtimes.sh
resolves each target to a concrete patch version at install time and
writes the result to resolved-runtimes.json. That resolved file, not this
one, is what a build is reproducible against.
A version bump here changes what candidate code runs on, so it changes
results. Treat it as a schema change: bump in a PR of its own, re-run the
regression bank against the M2 golden submissions, and record the before
and after in the PR body. Never bump during an open exam window.
ACTIVATES: M2 (2026-11-02 to 2026-11-27). Before then only the Piston
container itself runs; nothing calls it.

runtimes.notes: Default language for the coding bank and for every SQL-adjacent data question.
Matches the platform runtime, which keeps one Node version in a candidate's head and ours.
Compiles then runs. Compile time counts against EXEC_WALL_TIME_MS, not EXEC_CPU_TIME_MS.
JVM start-up dominates short programs. Sized in the pre-warm set for that reason.
Compiled per run; the compile step is the expensive half.
GCC. Compile errors must reach the candidate verbatim, which is why EXEC_MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES applies per stream.
Mono. Heaviest image in the matrix; install last.
Compile time regularly exceeds run time. Give rust questions a wall-time override.
Shares the JVM start-up cost with java and adds its own compile step.
Large image, low expected usage. Install it, do not pre-warm it.

How SQL questions execute. The question's schema and fixture rows are supplied as the stdin script; there is no server, no persistence and no network, which is exactly the isolation a SQL question needs.
